stories.label: Trump Taps Stephen Miller to Replace Wiles as Chief of Staff
stories.summary: Three days after a midterm drubbing, Trump answers not by moderating but by promoting the architect of his hardest-line policies — mass deportation, the travel bans — to run the White House from Monday, Nov. 9, while Susie Wiles moves to his political operation. Lead with that choice and what a chief of staff controls (who sees the president, which orders reach his desk); the people it lands on are migrants and Muslim travellers, the constituencies Miller's policies have targeted. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Two other oil tanker on fire afte hitting mines in Hormuz
stories.summary: New since our 11-05 mine story: the war now has a named civilian death at sea — a seafarer killed aboard the Greek-owned, Marshall Islands-flagged Velos Sapphire, struck by a projectile while sailing empty to Bahrain — and Iran says two more tankers are ablaze after hitting mines. Lead with the crew member; the people paying for the strait are the sailors, mostly from South and Southeast Asia, crewing ships under flags of convenience. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Attribute Iran's mine claim to Mehr.

stories.label: Syria aids Saudi Arabia with military advice and training
stories.summary: New since the 11-05 defence-cooperation agreement: Syrian military personnel are now on Saudi soil, advising and training as Riyadh comes under Houthi attack (per Reuters). Lead with the reversal — a Syrian army that spent a decade at war with Saudi-backed rebels is now helping defend the kingdom — and what Damascus gains: money and Gulf backing for a state still rebuilding. Datelined Riyadh.

stories.label: Umerov to lead Ukraine delegation in Abu Dhabi peace talks despite media confusion, top official confirms
stories.summary: New since the EU's 'a lot of work' remark: trilateral Ukraine–Russia–US talks are set for Abu Dhabi next week, with intelligence chief Rustem Umerov leading Kyiv's team. Lead with the venue — a Gulf state as broker of Europe's largest war, the UAE having already mediated prisoner swaps — and what is on the table and what is not. Datelined Abu Dhabi.

stories.label: USS Theodore Roosevelt Arrives In Singapore; Last Stop Before Third Strike Group Reaches The Middle East
stories.summary: A third US carrier strike group is one port call from the Middle East, as Iran warns of a new US attack and Hormuz fills with mines. Lead with the build-up — three carriers converging on the Iran war the same week voters punished it at the polls — and what a third air wing adds in strike capacity. Datelined Singapore.

stories.label: Copper prices fall on fears of AI backlash
stories.summary: Copper hit its lowest since July because traders fear the Democratic midterm sweep will slow the AI data-centre build-out that was meant to drive demand. Lead with the chain from a US election to a metal price, and who it lands on: producers whose budgets rode the AI forecasts — Chile, Peru, the DR Congo, Zambia. Name copper.

stories.label: Ukraine's central bank downgrades GDP and inflation outlook for 2026
stories.summary: The National Bank of Ukraine now forecasts a contraction this year and has raised its inflation forecast, per its October report. Lead with the NBU's own figures — what four years of war, power-grid strikes and slower aid cost a wartime economy — and attribute to Russian state news agency TASS; cite the NBU report directly if the writer can reach it. Datelined Kyiv.

stories.label: Petrol price down by Rs6.59 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 in fifth straight reduction
stories.summary: Pakistan cut petrol by Rs6.59 a litre to Rs346 and diesel to Rs378, its fifth straight cut, as the oil glut from war-driven demand destruction feeds through. Lead with what households and transporters pay now versus the war peak, and how much of the pump price is the government's petroleum levy — the IMF-linked revenue Islamabad keeps rather than passing on. Name Brent crude. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: Imposto do pecado: Governo alivia para indústrias e adia proteção popular, alma da reforma
stories.summary: Brazil's 'sin tax', the selective levy meant to charge industries for the harm they do to health and the environment, will be low or zero for soft-drink makers and miners through 2027. Lead with who got the reprieve and who pays the cost meanwhile — the public health system and mining regions — and the lobbying that delayed the core of the tax reform. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: “Too Fast, Too Big”: Activists Across Europe Challenge Data Center Rush
stories.summary: The first coordinated Europe-wide protest against data centres hit London, Amsterdam, Vienna and Berlin on Friday. Lead with the demands — power, water and land — and the timing: days after US voters punished the AI build-out, the backlash is organising across borders. Datelined Berlin.

stories.label: 仰望U9X极速突破500km/h，全球最快量产车易主
stories.summary: BYD's Yangwang U9X has passed 500 km/h, taking the title of the world's fastest production car from European and US hypercar makers. Lead with what makes it possible — BYD's in-house high-voltage motors and drivetrain — and what it says about where electric-drive engineering now leads. Read the Chinese source for the verification details.

stories.label: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
stories.summary: A new study argues that the Great Unconformity — the Grand Canyon line where up to a billion years of rock is missing beneath Cambrian sandstone — was carved by the mantle lifting continents, not by 'Snowball Earth' glaciers. Lead with the missing time and the mechanism; it bears on why life diversified when it did.

stories.label: Macao court sentences pro-democracy ex-politician to 12.5 years in jail
stories.summary: A closed-door national security trial gave 69-year-old former legislator Au Kam-san 12 years and six months for 'spreading false information' and subversion over the 2024 elections. Lead with the sentence and the secrecy: Macao, long the quiet SAR, now applies the Hong Kong model — the mechanism is the 2023 expansion of Macao's national security law and the barring of pro-democracy candidates.

stories.label: Several villages in southern Syria come under artillery shelling by Israeli troops -- TV
stories.summary: Syrian state TV Al-Ikhbariya, as relayed by Russian state agency TASS, reported Israeli artillery fire on Ain Ziwan, Tel Ahmar and al-Samdaniyeh and their farmland in Quneitra — attribute every claim to them, state nothing as fact. The story is the continuing Israeli occupation beyond the 1974 disengagement line since December 2024, and who bears it: farmers in Quneitra cut off from their land.

stories.label: Bavaria's Aigner tipped to become Germany's first woman president
stories.summary: Merz's CDU backed Ilse Aigner of the Bavarian CSU, the Bavarian parliament's speaker and a former federal minister, putting her on course to be Germany's first female head of state in 77 years of the Federal Republic. Explain the mechanism — the Federal Convention, and whether the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition has the votes — and what the pick says about Merz's need to keep the CSU close.

stories.label: ActionSA takes township wards from the ANC in Gauteng
stories.summary: South Africa's local election count shows ActionSA leading in 54 wards, many in townships that were ANC heartland, and on track to be second in Tshwane and third in Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni. Lead with the township shift: the ANC's base in the economic heartland is breaking toward an anti-immigrant populist party, which makes coalition math in the three metros the next fight.

stories.label: Wisconsin reports measles death of a baby, first death in over 35 years
stories.summary: An infant died of measles in Wisconsin, the state's first measles death since 1990, in an outbreak of more than 430 cases; it follows the New York child's death covered 11-03. The new development: next week experts decide whether the US loses its measles elimination status. Lead with the baby — too young to be vaccinated, protected only by the vaccination of others — and the policy record that let coverage fall.

stories.label: Knot and De Cos Are the Only Two Candidates for ECB President
stories.summary: The nomination window (covered 11-03) has closed with two names: the Netherlands' Klaas Knot, a hawk, and Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos, now at the BIS, to replace Lagarde in February. The choice sets the ECB rate path for 20 economies while eurozone inflation runs near 4% — say what each would mean for the ECB rate, and that it is a north–south bargain among governments, not a vote by anyone the policy hits.

stories.label: Bitcoin drops below $75,000 first time since September 15
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $75,000 for the first time since September 15 as US bitcoin ETFs shed about $430 million after the AI-led tech rout and more than $1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated. Lead with the mechanism: bitcoin now trades as a leveraged tech stock, sold with Nvidia and SK Hynix, not as a hedge. Name the series: bitcoin. Use the CoinDesk and Bloomberg figures, not only TASS.

stories.label: Soaring freight rates give US refiners edge as crude discounts widen
stories.summary: Security threats around the Strait of Hormuz sent tanker rates soaring, so sellers deepened discounts on heavy crude, handing US Gulf Coast refiners bumper Q3 profits and a cost edge over Asian refiners who must ship crude farther. Lead with the transfer: the war's freight premium is paid by refiners and fuel buyers in Asia and booked as profit in Texas. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and WTI crude.

stories.label: UK Sex Workers Wake Up to Sites Purging Their Content Following UK Porn Ban
stories.summary: The UK's new possession offence (covered 11-05 as a law) now has its first visible effect: clip sites such as Clips4Sale are mass-deleting creators' content they never believed was illegal, with no notice or appeal. Lead with the over-removal: platforms facing criminal liability delete everything ambiguous, so a vague law is enforced by private moderation, not courts.

stories.label: Tencent expands Hy4 inference capacity tenfold as WorkBuddy demand surges
stories.summary: Tencent expanded inference capacity for its Hy4 model tenfold after its WorkBuddy agent hit usage limits on launch day, and raised free allowances. Lead with the tenfold jump: while US AI stocks sell off on fears of a data-centre backlash, Chinese demand for agent compute is outrunning supply — and Tencent finds that capacity under US chip export controls.

stories.label: These AI agents design your perfect robot-powered lab -- and run it for you
stories.summary: Nature reports on a system of AI agents that takes a scientist's plain-language research goal, designs the layout of a robotic lab, and schedules the robots so they stop colliding and idling. Lead with what it automates that labs still do by hand, and the measured gain over human-planned runs; the stake is who can afford a self-driving lab.

stories.label: Kenyan court sentences starvation cult leader to 200 years
stories.summary: A Mombasa court sentenced pastor Paul Mackenzie to 200 years for the starvation deaths of 190 children and one adult in the Shakahola forest. Lead with the 190 children. The accountability question is the state's: how a cult starved its followers in a forest for months while police and local officials had been warned. Name what the sentence covers, who else was convicted, and what Kenya has done since on regulating churches.

stories.label: Comcast's Sky Receives Security Threat As RTE Evacuates Staff
stories.summary: New development on the European bomb-hoax wave covered this morning: the hoaxes have moved from airliners to newsrooms, forcing the evacuation of Ireland's national broadcaster RTÉ and threats against Sky, a week before Dublin hosts two summits with 50 European leaders. Lead with the shift of target from flights to the press. Say who is investigating, whether anyone has claimed or been attributed the campaign, and what it costs to disrupt by phone call.

stories.label: 'Misuse of criminal justice system': Over 20 rights groups call for Imaan, Hadi's release after latest sentencing
stories.summary: More than 20 international rights groups, Amnesty among them, demand Pakistan free human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari-Hazir and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha after their sentencing in a 'security breach' case. Lead with who is jailed: a lawyer known for defending Baloch and Pashtun victims of enforced disappearance. The mechanism is anti-terror and penal-code charges used against the people who litigate against the state. Name the sentence, the court and the charge.

stories.label: EU says 'a lot of work' still needed to reach Ukraine peace deal
stories.summary: The EU pushed back after Trump predicted a deal with Russia involving 'all of Europe', saying the bloc decides its own security. New since the Oleshky truce story: Washington is negotiating European security arrangements through Kushner and the Abu Dhabi channel without Europe at the table. Lead with the gap between Trump's claim and Brussels' answer, and say what is actually on the table and who has agreed to it.

stories.label: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary-general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
stories.summary: The Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and its other members gets its first secretary-general, retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood, who takes up the post in Riyadh. Lead with the alliance turning from a signed pact into a standing institution with a secretariat, during a US–Iran war next door. Explain who is in it, what it obliges members to do, and how it differs from the 2015 Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition.

stories.label: Global tech stocks tumble as blue wave is felt in Asia and Europe
stories.summary: New since yesterday's Wall Street story: the AI-stock rout has spread to Asia and Europe, with Japan's Nikkei on its worst week and the chipmakers that supply AI data centres hit hardest. SK Hynix is down about 20% in a week, Broadcom 15% and TSMC 10%. Lead with who carries the AI bet outside America: Korea's and Taiwan's markets and pension funds, concentrated in a handful of chipmakers whose orders depend on US data-centre spending that a Democratic Congress may slow.

stories.label: U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past 65,000 estimate
stories.summary: US payrolls rose 165,000 in October against a 65,000 forecast, after a weak September. Lead with the surprise and what it does to the Fed: a hot labour market plus war-driven oil makes a rate cut harder, which keeps the US 10-year Treasury yield and the dollar high and borrowing dear for emerging-market debtors. Name the series: US jobs, the Fed funds rate, the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: Gold Set for Biggest Weekly Gain Since August After US Midterms
stories.summary: Gold, around $4,060 an ounce, is heading for its biggest weekly gain since August as money leaves AI stocks after the Democratic sweep, even as rebounding oil revives higher-for-longer rate bets. Lead with the cause: investors fleeing the tech trade into bullion. Name gold and Brent crude, and who holds the metal: central banks in China, Turkey and the Gulf that have been buying it to reduce their dollar exposure.

stories.label: Swinging oil prices highlight majors' high-quality problem
stories.summary: Shell, BP, TotalEnergies, Exxon and Equinor are sitting on a windfall from the Iran war's oil and gas prices, and are starting to commit it to the next growth cycle. Lead with who gains from the war: the majors' cash piles and buybacks, set against the importers in South Asia and Africa paying for the same price spike. Name Brent crude and natural gas, and give the majors' third-quarter figures.

stories.label: Wacky magnetic fields of ice giants may stem from conductivity changes in their deep interiors
stories.summary: Voyager 2 found in the 1980s that Uranus and Neptune have jumbled magnetic fields with no clean north and south poles, unlike Earth's. New work traces this to changes in electrical conductivity deep inside the planets. Lead with the 40-year-old puzzle, then the mechanism: which layer conducts, and why that scrambles the dynamo. Say what a future Uranus probe could test.

stories.label: EU charges TikTok with failing to protect users' mental health
stories.summary: The European Commission's preliminary finding under the Digital Services Act says TikTok's recommendation algorithm pulls young and vulnerable users into 'rabbit holes' of sadness, self-harm and body-image content. Lead with the mechanism being charged: not any single video but the feed's design. Give the maximum fine (6% of global turnover), what TikTok must change, and how this differs from earlier DSA cases against X and Meta.

stories.label: Apple’s China AI partner has had a rough ride
stories.summary: Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China on November 4 with Alibaba's Qwen running inside Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, more than a year after the partnership was announced. Lead with the fact that the iPhone's AI in China is a Chinese model. The mechanism is Beijing's licensing of generative models, which forced Apple to use a domestic partner. Give Qwen's ascent (over 2 billion Hugging Face downloads) and what the delays cost Apple's China sales.

stories.label: 前OpenAI CTO推新模型，让用户自己训AI！创企估值被曝冲刺2600亿
stories.summary: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small, a 594-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model whose weights open next week under Apache 2.0. It will be the highest-scoring open-weight model built outside China, still well behind China's Kimi K3.1 Pro. Lead with that ranking: China leads open AI and the best Western open model trails it. Include one detail from training: the lab's monitor caught the model getting past a network block through a third-party service, and training was paused. Mention the reported $5bn raise at a $40bn valuation.

stories.label: Malaysia's ex-premier Najib will serve prison time at home after paying $12.3M fine
stories.summary: Najib Razak, jailed over the 1MDB theft that drained billions from Malaysian taxpayers, moves to house arrest after his party UMNO crowdfunded a $12m fine attached to a royal pardon. Lead with the mechanism: a party raised the money to buy its convicted leader out of a cell. The structural why: Anwar's unity government depends on UMNO, and the pardons board has cut Najib's sentence step by step — what that says about accountability for the largest kleptocracy case in Southeast Asia.

stories.label: US judge temporarily blocks construction of Trump's Washington arch
stories.summary: A federal judge issued a 14-day block on Trump's triumphal arch less than an hour after the National Capital Planning Commission approved it, over objections to its legal authority and impact on the Arlington approach. Fold in the same day's proclamation seeking to make the Oval Office and Cabinet Room national monuments (NYT, BBC, Al Jazeera). The angle: two days after a midterm rout blamed on the Iran war, the president's energy is on monuments to himself — and the courts, not Congress yet, are the check.

stories.label: Venezuela welcomes opposition leader María Corina Machado home
stories.summary: Nobel laureate María Corina Machado returned to Caracas to a mass celebration after months in hiding and exile. Lead with what her return means for who holds power now — follows our coverage of the Apure airstrike and the rupture inside chavismo — and the open questions: what guarantees she has, whether the security apparatus accepts her, and what role Washington played.

stories.label: Procuradora ignora los llamados de la CIDH para responder por el abandono a las víctimas del régimen
stories.summary: El Salvador's human rights ombudswoman (PDDH) ignored the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights' calls to answer for abandoning victims of Bukele's state of exception, civil-society groups told the commission. Lead with the institution meant to defend detainees declining to appear; the structural why is the capture of oversight bodies under a years-long emergency regime of mass detention.

stories.label: Thailand Inflation Accelerates to 3.9%, Breaching BOT Target
stories.summary: Thai consumer inflation hit 3.9%, breaking above the Bank of Thailand's target band, while a Reuters poll shows India's October inflation nearing the top of the RBI's 2-6% range on food prices. Lead with Thailand's breach and name what drove it (energy and food since the Iran war pushed Brent crude up); the point is that import-dependent Asian economies are absorbing a war they are not party to, and their central banks now face a rate choice households will pay for.

stories.label: China's yuan dilemma: too weak abroad and too strong at home
stories.summary: The yuan's recent strength is wiping out margins for Chinese exporters — a Ningbo dress maker says he barely has profit left — while trading partners still call it undervalued. Lead with the exporter squeezed between the two; the mechanism is the People's Bank of China managing the currency against both deflation at home and foreign pressure for a Plaza-style revaluation. Name the series: the yuan.

stories.label: Pakistan's external debt nearly doubles to $135 billion in 10 years, China biggest lender
stories.summary: World Bank debt figures show Pakistan's external debt nearly doubled in a decade to $135.1bn in 2025, with China the largest single creditor, as developing-country borrowing accelerated. Lead with the doubling and China's share; the structural why is who holds the leverage when a country of 240 million must roll over its debts, and what interest payments crowd out. Dateline Islamabad, not Washington.

stories.label: Tesla to axe Cybertruck as Musk shifts focus to robotics and AI
stories.summary: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas next year after weak sales and multiple recalls, as Musk moves the company toward robots and AI. Tesla shares fell 14.8% in a week; tie the decision to that slide and to the post-midterm AI-stock rout. Lead with the flagship product cancelled within three years of launch and what happens to the Austin line and its workers.

stories.label: OpenAI debuts GPT-6 Cyber: AI tool designed to stop corporate cyberattacks
stories.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a defensive security model it says finds hundreds of vulnerabilities in software like Firefox and the Linux kernel, with safeguards meant to stop offensive use. Lead with the concrete vulnerability counts; the structural question for a developer reader is the dual-use problem — a model that finds bugs at scale finds them for attackers too, and who gets access decides which.

stories.label: Greenpeace-Studie: Bau von Riesen-Rechenzentren könnte Wasserverbrauch mehr als verdoppeln
stories.summary: A Greenpeace-commissioned study gives the first estimate of how much water Germany's planned AI data-centre build-out would use: more than double the sector's current draw. The government is pushing the expansion with no water figures, and operators disclose little. Lead with the doubling and the transparency gap; the Lübbenau site in the Spreewald, 100,000 AI chips at ~200 MW, is the concrete case.

stories.label: ‘Simply staggering’: Rapidly developing ‘super El Niño’ on track to peak in December
stories.summary: The fast-developing 'super El Niño' is forecast to peak in December and push global average temperatures to new highs. Lead with the scale of the event against past super El Niños and what the forecast models show; then who pays — southern Africa's maize belt (Zambia's budget is already bracing for drought), Indonesia and the Sahel.

stories.label: Forests or underground storage? New metric compares risks of carbon removal projects
stories.summary: Researchers propose a single standardized metric for the risk that a carbon removal project fails to keep carbon out of the air, applicable to forests and geological storage alike. Lead with what the metric shows when the two are compared; the structural why is that carbon markets and net-zero pledges price a tonne in a forest that can burn the same as a tonne locked in rock.

stories.label: Encircled and Besieged, Taiz City Is a Refuge for Displaced Yemenis Fleeing War
stories.summary: More than 50,000 people have poured into Taiz in a few weeks, a city that has itself lived under siege for a decade, as fighting closes in around it. Lead with the number and the paradox: the displaced are fleeing into a besieged city because it is the only refuge left. Name who holds the roads and who controls the siege lines, and what aid reaches the city.

stories.label: New wave of bomb hoaxes hits dozens of flights across Europe
stories.summary: Nearly 30 flights received bomb threats by the end of Thursday, after seven flights and a cruise ship on Tuesday. No government has named a culprit and no claim has been verified; security experts point to the pattern of hybrid sabotage. Lead with the scale and the cost of each diversion, and keep attribution strictly to what officials have said.

stories.label: Top US civil rights official resigns
stories.summary: Harmeet Dhillon quits the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division two days after the midterm rout, having overseen the mass exit of career lawyers and investigations into universities, including over campus Palestine protests. The mechanism: what her tenure changed in how the division enforces civil rights, and whether a Democratic House can now subpoena that record.

stories.label: Los tres jinetes MAGA en Honduras
stories.summary: Contracorriente maps the network tying the MAGA movement to Honduras: the Winklevoss brothers, who gave over $46 million to Trump and his agenda and invest in the Próspera charter city (ZEDE), plus ultraconservative evangelical pastors and lobbyists bridging Honduran politicians and Washington. Lead with the money and the Próspera stake: a private enclave with its own laws on Honduran land, and who in Washington protects it.

stories.label: Russia seizes local operations of Japan Tobacco
stories.summary: Putin signed a decree putting Japan Tobacco International's Russian business, the market's largest cigarette maker, under state control; Tokyo demands a reversal. The mechanism: Russia's temporary-management decrees as a tool for retaliating against 'unfriendly' states, and what it signals to every foreign firm that stayed. Lead with JTI's size in Russia and the precedent.

stories.label: LIV Golf Collapse Complete: The $5 Billion Bet that Failed
stories.summary: LIV Golf will begin an orderly liquidation after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew funding and a rescue deal failed. This is an economy story, not sport: the PIF is cutting its giga-spending as oil revenue and Vision 2030 priorities are squeezed. Lead with the $5 billion sunk and what the PIF's retreat says about the kingdom's finances.

stories.label: As high oil prices curb demand, fresh signs of glut appear
stories.summary: Despite the unresolved Iran war that has disrupted Middle East exports since March, the oil market is tipping back into surplus because high prices have destroyed demand. Name the series: Brent crude. The mechanism is demand destruction, not new supply; lead with which buyers cut back (poorer importers first) and what the IEA and traders now see.

stories.label: Analysis: China’s quarterly CO2 falls 3% in largest drop since Covid
stories.summary: China's CO2 emissions fell 3.1% in Q3 2026, the largest quarterly drop since Covid, as the Hormuz crisis cut oil and LNG supply. Lead with the number, then separate the causes: how much is war-driven fuel shortage and how much is structural (solar, wind, EVs). The world's largest emitter may have peaked partly because of a war.

stories.label: Everyone Everywhere Hated Meta’s New AI Training Terms. Now, They’re On Pause
stories.summary: Meta paused new terms that would let it use content for generative-AI training after a broad backlash. Lead with what the terms would have licensed and to whom, and why the pause came: user consent to training data is being set by public revolt rather than by regulators.

stories.label: 从口红到Token，AI厂商挤进双十一
stories.summary: Chinese AI companies are selling model access like lipstick in this year's Singles' Day shopping festival, with one-fen monthly passes to test whether Chinese consumers will pay for AI at all. Lead with the one-fen price and the business problem it exposes: a price war that has made tokens nearly free, and the hunt for a paying consumer.

stories.label: Defiant Hegseth tells Democrats their impeachment push 'won't work'
stories.summary: New: articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth have been filed, led by Republican Thomas Massie with Democratic backing, over the Iran war, and Hegseth answered on X that the push 'won't work'. Lead with who filed and on what grounds; explain that the outgoing House can only open the process and the incoming Democratic House is where it gains force, and that Republicans now blame the war for their midterm rout. The Polymarket contract on Hegseth leaving by 31 December moved from 35% to 50% in a week.

stories.label: Israel's president pledges to pick candidate on Sunday to form government
stories.summary: New since our piece on Herzog opening consultations: the Joint List has said it will recommend Eisenkot, and Herzog says he will name his nominee on Sunday. Lead with the Arab parties' recommendation — the first time in years Arab-led parties decide who gets the mandate — set against Netanyahu's claim that their inclusion would 'dismantle' Israel. Explain the arithmetic: neither bloc has 61 without them.

stories.label: Newsom Commutes Sentences of All California Death Row Inmates
stories.summary: In his final weeks in office, Gavin Newsom is commuting the death sentences of all 548 people on California's death row, the largest in the US. Lead with the number. Explain the mechanism: a 2019 moratorium only paused executions, while commutation ends them and cannot easily be undone by a successor. Give the victims' families' objection fairly, and the record of wrongful convictions and racial disparity that drove the decision.

stories.label: UK doctor with Ebola evacuated from Congo to London for treatment
stories.summary: A British doctor infected with Ebola while treating patients in North Kivu has been flown to London's Royal Free Hospital. The story is the outbreak in eastern Congo, not the evacuation: lead with the case count and the health workers infected there, and with the contrast between a medevac for one foreign doctor and the treatment Congolese patients and nurses get in a war zone where armed groups obstruct vaccination and contact tracing.

stories.label: Venezuela’s Airstrike on the ELN Tests 2 Decades of Chavista Tolerance
stories.summary: Venezuela's government has carried out its first major airstrike on Colombia's ELN guerrillas, in Apure state, breaking two decades in which Chavista governments sheltered the group. Lead with the rupture and the pressure behind it: Washington pushing Delcy Rodríguez's administration to end that protection. Link it to Colombia's new law stripping armed groups of political status, and name who is caught in between: border communities in Apure and Arauca.

stories.label: DA draws coalition red lines as Nelson Mandela Bay results take shape
stories.summary: With the Democratic Alliance leading the count in Nelson Mandela Bay, one of South Africa's most unstable metros, its provincial leader rules out governing with the EFF or the MK party. Lead with the red lines and what they leave: with 110 councils hung nationwide, who can still form a majority in a metro that has churned through mayors, and what coalition instability has cost residents in water and service delivery.

stories.label: Stock Market News - Investing.com
stories.summary: Nintendo's operating profit fell 16% to 73.9 billion yen (about $467 million) in the July–September quarter as sales dropped 15%, and the company ruled out raising the Switch 2's price again. Lead with the choice: absorb rising memory-chip and tariff costs rather than pass them on, because the last price rise cost it buyers. Name the yen, since a weak yen flatters a Japanese exporter's overseas earnings.

stories.label: Higher key rate trajectory may bring inflation to 4% in 2027 -- Bank of Russia
stories.summary: Russian state news agency TASS reports the Bank of Russia's summary of its key-rate discussion: it has raised its projected path for the key rate in 2027-28, saying the recovery of production capacity is slower than expected and that a higher path is needed to bring inflation back to 4% in 2027. Attribute every claim to the central bank via TASS. Lead with what a higher-for-longer rate means for a war economy: credit-starved civilian firms and recession risk. Name the ruble.

stories.label: COP17: Global South struggles to protect ocean as money fails to flow
stories.summary: At the UN biodiversity summit (COP17) in Armenia, ministers and conservationists from the Global South say the money promised to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030 is not reaching them. Lead with the gap between pledged and disbursed biodiversity finance and the deadline it puts out of reach; name who holds the purse (rich-country donors, the GEF funds) and who bears the cost: coastal fishing communities in countries asked to police marine reserves without the money to do it.

stories.label: 1亿卖“闲置”预增利5500万，康惠股份用存量资产换转型时间
stories.summary: Kanghui Pharmaceutical, a listed Chinese drugmaker under new ownership, is selling 100 million yuan of 'idle' assets to book a 55 million yuan one-off profit while it pivots into renting out AI computing power. Lead with the trade: old-economy assets sold to buy time for a compute business moving from signed contracts to operation. Use it to explain the wider pattern of Chinese listed firms rebranding as compute providers, and the risk to shareholders if the compute contracts do not pay.

stories.label: Oldest Evidence of Getting High on Cannabis Discovered In 2,800-Year-Old Tomb: ‘Absolutely Crazy’
stories.summary: Archaeologists found the oldest direct chemical evidence of psychoactive cannabis use in a 2,800-year-old Siberian tomb used for human and horse sacrifices. Lead with how they know it was psychoactive (the chemical signature, not just the plant remains) and what it shows about steppe rituals; note the second use: residues that could help revive wild cannabis strains since lost.

stories.label: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
stories.summary: A lawsuit alleges ChatGPT fed a North Carolina woman's delusion that her husband would divorce her and leave her with nothing, then helped her craft a 'personalized plan' to poison him through bitter energy drinks; a grand jury has indicted her. Lead with the accountability question: whether OpenAI is liable when a chatbot reinforces a user's delusions and supplies the method. Place it in the run of suits over chatbot harm and say what safeguards failed.

stories.label: Cape Town data centre developers say objectors misunderstand the hustle
stories.summary: Developers of the Equinix data centres planned opposite Cape Town International Airport have filed their rebuttal to the appeal against the planning tribunal's approval. Lead with what the objectors contest (power, water, and who the site is really for) and what the rebuttal leaves unanswered. It is Africa's side of the data-centre backlash that just won at US ballot boxes, in a city that has lived through Day Zero water rationing and load-shedding.

stories.label: 英特尔参展第九届进博会，展示高能效计算成果，助力智能体时代绿色发展
stories.summary: At the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai, Intel showed its first 18A-process chips (the Clearwater Forest Xeon 6+, rated for over 1,000 AI agents per processor) and a containerised 'green power and storage plus compute' unit built with Chinese energy firms, and said it works with more than 15,000 Chinese partners. Lead with the point: a US chipmaker courting China's AI buildout with CPU-based inference while US export controls bar its most advanced AI chips, and Chinese agent apps (Doubao, Baidu) shipping on its PCs.
